plan.cache_estimate: Every workflow differs from rev1 (the routing question is in every workflow and every reading request), so the routing and reading calls are all new; only document-finder turns that open with an unchanged process reference and identical tool results can come from the cache. Estimate: every call new, at the higher of the per-file cost of the clean arm and of the rev1 re-run per regime (upper bound).
plan.decision: Estimate exceeds USD 0.60: whole regimes in the order dismissal, theft, tenancy; launching stops when the ledger total reaches before + 0.60; only complete regimes are reported as such.

closing: Product behaviour that remains, by size, in errors per file over the two complete regimes (theft and dismissal, 114 files; tenancy ran 28 of 59 files and is not a regime figure): (1) supplied-document judgments, 24 errors, 0.21 per file: sufficient documents judged insufficient (9), findings the second judgment or the source checker did not confirm (8), present documents judged missing (4), and three the other way; not re-reviewed against the rewritten must_show items, so some may be text against recorded state; (2) stated facts held because one reading's quotation was not found word for word (a capital letter, scan noise corrected), 14 errors, 0.12 per file, most of them on defining events that hold a whole type; (3) stated facts held because one reading of three answered otherwise (household member, vouchers, incapacity, probation, order of notice and protected period), about 12 errors, 0.11 per file, of which the_248aa95805a8's household reading (4) is the open reading also seen in rev0 and 5 more are carried over as text against recorded state; (4) routing, 12 errors, 0.11 per file: 5 in two theft files whose defining event is designed open (benchmark design) and 7 in three dismissal wrongful_termination files routed to protected_period_notice or left unrouted under the revised routing question, which the next design cycle should read before any further wording change. No run failed.
